So, I've been dating this girl for a few months, and she's 18. She wears makeupâĢĶfoundation, blusher, fills in her eyebrows and eyelashes. I know she does this, and I don't like it when she wears all of that at once. But I don't want to control her, so I only tell her if it looks bad or something. That makes sense because I don't want her to feel bad about how she looks. The other day, we went into town, and she kept asking me to take my hat off. She eventually said it made her feel embarrassed and literally said that it's silly for a 23-year-old man to be wearing an neon purple hat with "Pierce the Veil" on it (which is a band). She said I should have already grown out of this phase, which I found very insulting because the hat is a way of expressing my identity. So, I just said nothing, calmly looked her in the eye, and said, "Well, your makeup is overdone." She was quiet for a minute and then told me I was being an immature asshole, and that it's normal for her to wear "subtle makeup" but not normal for me to wear my hat. We haven't really spoken since, and she's clearly annoyed, but I think I was pointing out a very clear double standard. So, if I'm an asshole, then she's an asshole as well. But now I'm wondering, did I do the right thing? Is it okay to call her out on the double standard, or was I being too harsh? I don't want to hurt her feelings, but I also don't want to be controlled or made to feel bad about how I express myself. Maybe I should think about how she feels. She's 18, and maybe she's insecure about her appearance, which is why she wears makeup. I don't like it when she wears a lot of makeup, but I don't want to make her feel bad about it. On the other hand, she's telling me to take off my hat, which is something I use to express myself. It's a part of who I am. I guess the issue is that she's criticizing me for something that's important to me, and I'm criticizing her for something she's doing. It seems like a double standard because she's okay with her makeup but not with my hat. But is it really a double standard? Or is it just that we have different things that are important to us? Maybe I should communicate more about why the hat is important to me and why I don't like her wearing a lot of makeup. But I don't want to come off as controlling or critical. I just want us to respect each other's choices. I also wonder if there's a better way to address the double standard without making her feel attacked. Maybe instead of saying her makeup is overdone, I could have talked about how I feel when she tells me to take off my hat. That way, it's more about my feelings and less about judging her. But in the moment, I was upset because she made me feel like I was childish for wearing the hat. So, I reacted by pointing out her makeup. It was a defensive move, but I don't know if it was the best approach. I also think about whether it's okay to have different standards for ourselves and our partners. Maybe it's normal to have things that we're okay with in ourselves but not in others, but it's important to communicate that in a respectful way. Overall, I'm not sure if I did the right thing. I want to stand up for myself and express my identity, but I also don't want to hurt her or create conflict in our relationship. Maybe I should reflect on how I can address these issues more constructively in the future.
